common_name: Champagne Elegance Bearded Iris (Reblooming Soft Beige-Pink Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and well-drained soil; Champagne Elegance is a widely grown reblooming bearded iris known for a second flush of bloom in fall.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil, never burying them completely. Champagne Elegance bears soft, blended beige-pink standards and falls with a warm, glowing quality that reads almost peach in some light, and it is one of the most dependable reblooming bearded iris cultivars available, often producing a second flush of flowers in late summer or fall in addition to its main spring bloom. Its gentle, warm coloring pairs easily with almost any companion planting. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years after bloom, and keep the rhizomes in full sun with sharp drainage to avoid rot; light feeding after each bloom cycle helps support reliable reblooming.

common_name: Gypsy Lord Bearded Iris (Blue-and-Purple Bitone Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and well-drained soil; Gypsy Lord is a bitone bearded iris pairing lighter blue standards with deeper violet-purple falls.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil, never burying them completely. Gypsy Lord bears lighter blue-violet standards over deeper, richer purple falls, a classic bitone color pattern on large, ruffled blooms held on tall, sturdy stems well above the fan of foliage. Its bold, saturated coloring and strong garden performance have kept it popular among bearded iris growers for mixed borders and cutting. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years after bloom, and keep the rhizomes in full sun with sharp drainage to avoid rot.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and well-drained soil; Thornbird bears an intricate tan-and-lavender veined pattern typical of the finest modern bearded iris breeding.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil, never burying them completely. Thornbird bears warm tan-gold standards over falls delicately veined and washed with lavender-violet, an intricate, softly blended pattern characteristic of modern exhibition-quality bearded iris breeding, opening on tall, well-branched stems. Its subtle, complex coloring rewards close viewing and pairs beautifully with both warm and cool-toned companion plantings. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years after bloom, and keep the rhizomes in full sun with sharp drainage to avoid rot.
